name: What signs mean my pool deck should be remodeled with the pool?

mainEntity.name: What signs mean my pool deck should be remodeled with the pool?
mainEntity.text: What signs mean my pool deck should be remodeled with the pool?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pool deck should usually be remodeled with the pool when it has cracking, heaving, ponding water, poor drainage, slippery surfaces, or separation from the coping. These issues are not just cosmetic. They can affect safety, water management, and the performance of surrounding finishes. If the deck is failing, remodeling only the pool interior may leave the overall project looking incomplete. Water that drains badly around the pool can also contribute to staining, erosion, and repeat damage near the shell edge. In many Los Angeles remodels, deck work becomes the smart add-on because crews are already on site and the pool is already open. Homeowners should ask whether the deck condition is causing or contributing to the pool’s problems. In some cases, only a small section needs repair. In others, a larger rebuild is more cost-effective and produces a better final result. A good contractor will explain whether the deck is structurally sound, cosmetically tired, or both.
acceptedAnswer.description: If the pool deck is cracked, uneven, slippery, poorly draining, or pulling away from the coping, it should usually be evaluated with the pool remodel. Deck problems often affect safety, drainage, and the long-term performance of new coping or tile, so fixing only the pool surface may leave major issues behind.
